LESSON: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should one read for main ideas? 2. How can you improve your reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify reading strategies for use on given texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. select main ideas and details from written texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge reading for main ideas and details as a comprehension skill. ● In pairs, guide the learners to search online and watch appropriate audio-visual clips on the selected reading strategies: reading for main ideas and reading for details,learners with blindness to use digital devices with assistive technology. ● Learners are guided to read and highlight the main ideas and details in texts on consumer roles and responsibilities and review each other’s work. ● Learners are guided to share ideas on how one can practically use the selected reading strategies. ● In pairs, guide the learners with low vision to complete the substitution tables with specific details from texts. Learners with blindness use a braille substitution table with embossed outlines. ● Let the learner with low vision complete a mind map and learners with blindness read the description of the mind map with focus on the main idea and details. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: The learner shares what they have learnt while completing the mind map prompting desire to learn

more. .

● Digital literacy: The learner manipulates digital devices when searching online and watching appropriate video clips on the

selected reading strategies.

Values:
Unity: A learner enhances this value as they work together in groups and pairs to complete the mind map.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Consumer literacy skills: The learner reads and underlines the main ideas and details in texts on consumer roles and

responsibilities which enhances consumer literacy skills.

Main points to remember:
